correspondence.component_scope: Southern opening and northward plateau corridor west of Yaminué
correspondence.finding: The source depicts plateau terrain east of the separately labeled Arroyo Comicó and west of the separately labeled Arroyo Seco Yaminué, near La Quebrada and Estancia Serra. The selected route follows this intervening plateau northward. The original does not establish a continuous mapped drainage along this substantial upper corridor or its complete northward connection to the Corral Chico lowland.
correspondence.correspondence: Terrain setting established; material hydrographic correspondence remains unresolved.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Small isolated wet depressions occur nearby. Neither those depressions nor adjacent Comicó/Yaminué channels establish the selected upper connection. No reservoir is depicted in the selected opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Ministro Ramos Mexía transport crossing and Laguna Corral Chico transition
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor reaches the western side of Ministro Ramos Mexía, crosses the road/rail belt, and approaches the southern/eastern side of the mapped Laguna Corral Chico depression. The original depicts the lagoon and a northeastward intermittent drainage from that setting, but it does not establish the incoming connection from the southern plateau as a complete watercourse.
correspondence.correspondence: Settlement, crossing, lagoon and outgoing northeast corridor established; the upper-to-lagoon drainage link remains a material gap.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Laguna Corral Chico is a material mapped depression on the selected corridor. Its name is not extended to the river group. Nearby lagunas Lauriente, Vicente, Comezana and Marín Camino are distinct features, not inferred selected lake passages.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeast intermittent drainage by Laguna El Gateado and the S. Ruiz–Caita Toro setting
correspondence.finding: The original depicts the northeast-running intermittent channel from the Corral Chico area, its relation to the eastern side of Laguna El Gateado, and continuation past the S. Ruiz estancia toward Caita Toro. Multiple small lateral intermittent branches and wet hollows are drawn. The connected corridor can be followed without assigning those side branches a common hydronym.
correspondence.correspondence: Established at generalized channel/depression and local junction scale.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: El Gateado is a named lagoon setting adjoining the selected drainage. No present water level or permanent lagoon-to-channel flow is asserted; no reservoir is depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: Santa Rosa lowland and unnamed eastward drainage north of Loma China Muerta
correspondence.finding: The mapped channel continues northeast and then east by Santa Rosa. An elongated intermittently wetted hollow and parallel/branching drainage traces occur immediately east of the estancia. The corridor continues along the northern side of Loma China Muerta, receiving small lateral branches before the major southward turn. The separately mapped Bajo Rico, Salitral Negro and northern branch network are contextual neighboring components; they are not assigned a selected trunk name.
correspondence.correspondence: Established at ordinary lowland/channel and branch-junction scale, without exact selection of banks or parallel wetland strands.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Unnamed wet lowland at Santa Rosa is material. No dam or reservoir is depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward lower channel into northern Bajo de Valcheta
correspondence.finding: The original shows the eastward drainage gathering with northern and eastern intermittent branches, then turning south through a narrow vegetated channel corridor east of Loma China Muerta. It bends east at the edge of the Tres Picos depression. This is the northern approach to Tres Picos, spatially separate from the Arroyo Nahuel Niyeu wetland belt approaching the saline-lagoon complex from the southwest.
correspondence.correspondence: Established for the lower channel, material convergence and lagoon approach.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Natural channel and lowland approach, with no reservoir or dam depicted. Arroyo Nahuel Niyeu is a neighboring receiving-drainage label on a different route and is not a representative candidate for this selected northern approach.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual inland terminal in Laguna Tres Picos
correspondence.finding: The selected lower route enters the northwestern/northern part of the crosshatched saline depression labeled Laguna Tres Picos and ends within it. Laguna Indio Muerto is a separate mapped neighboring lagoon farther east/southeast. The endpoint is not moved to Indio Muerto merely because that name is used for a larger regional basin.
correspondence.correspondence: Actual terminal setting established at saline-lagoon-complex scale.
correspondence.lakes_wetlands_reservoirs: Laguna Tres Picos is the selected natural saline-lagoon terminal. No sea outlet, reservoir, exact shoreline or present permanent inundation is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Selected eastern headward lake and southern transfer toward Inulik Lake
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies in the small elongated unnamed lake immediately east of Inulik Lake, printed with a 1504-foot elevation. The map distinguishes this lake from the lower-elevation, broadly lobed Inulik Lake. Its westward outlet and the intervening stream/pond setting can be seen. The selected route instead proceeds southwest from the lake's southern part into Inulik's southeastern waterbody; that selected transfer cannot be securely read as a continuous mapped connection at this source scale.
correspondence.limits: This is a lake-to-lake route question, not a demand for exact bank or vertex agreement. The visible alternative westward drainage is not used to replace the selected southern transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Inulik Lake traverse and northward Tree River outlet
correspondence.finding: The broad southern and northwestern parts of Inulik Lake account for the selected westward lake traverse and northward bend. Its outlet is directly labelled Tree River and passes through short lake expansions and a falls/rapids reach before continuing across the adjoining sheet boundary. The large Takijuq Lake to the south is a separate regional feature, not a selected passage.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper Tree River eastward lake and short-channel sequence
correspondence.finding: South of the separately labelled Kikerk Lake, the selected corridor follows the Tree River's chain of irregular lake expansions and short channels eastward. The original distinguishes the selected southern/eastward continuation from adjacent north-trending lake arms and feeder streams. Rapids and falls are shown along parts of this chain. The corridor turns northeast into the elongated lake-and-river valley farther east.
correspondence.limits: No name is independently established for every selected lake expansion or tributary. Kikerk Lake is a sheet/adjacent-lake label, not a blanket selected-route name.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeast Tree River trunk and major lake passages
correspondence.finding: The northeast-trending selected line corresponds to the connected long lake expansions and Tree River reaches in the eastern part of 86P, including the large lake printed with a 718-foot elevation and its northeast outlet reach. The lower river continues across the sheet edge onto 76M, with several side streams and nearby parallel valleys distinguishable from the selected trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Tree River and actual coastal terminal
correspondence.finding: The labelled lower Tree River continues northeast through the valley, turns toward the head of Port Epworth and reaches the inlet's southern end. Port Epworth opens northward into Coronation Gulf. The selected terminal is therefore supported at the river-to-inlet setting; neither a neighboring eastward river nor the more distant gulf shoreline is substituted for the actual terminal.
correspondence.prose_scope: The same sheet's fish-resource commentary independently discusses the lower Tree River, a falls approximately 9 km upstream of its mouth, and fishing at its mouth. This prose corroborates the named lower-river setting but does not resolve the initial lake transfer.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern headward opening and initial southwest descent
correspondence.finding: The model begins in the east and trends southwest to an initial westward corridor. Its actual source waterbody, terrain, significant tributary junctions and any lake or ice association are unestablished from allowed original cartography.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper westward corridor and shallow northward return
correspondence.finding: The model continues broadly west with a shallow northward return before turning southwest again. This geometric orientation does not establish the actual channel, lake passages, branches or hydronym.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle westward course and southwestern bend
correspondence.finding: The model follows a broad westward corridor, then bends southwest. No allowed original map establishes the middle course, its material junctions or any transfer through a lake.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southwestward descent
correspondence.finding: The model continues southwest toward the retained coastal terminal classification. Its actual lower river identity, branch configuration and lake links remain without map correspondence.

correspondence.component_scope: Terminal approach and actual receiving water
correspondence.finding: The modeled ending turns west and then southwest into the retained sea-classified terminal. The actual receiving bay or sea, connection from the lower route and terminal setting have not been established from allowed primary map pixels. The retained sea classification is not independent evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Headward opening and southward upper corridor
correspondence.finding: Selected geometry shows a southward opening west of Lake Hazen. The lawfully read park index supplies only broad regional terrain and ice context. No original source establishes the selected opening’s actual ice/rock setting, named glacier, surface stream or subglacial continuity.

correspondence.component_scope: Western feeder, southern bend and eastward middle corridor
correspondence.finding: Selected geometry runs southeast and then east toward the Lake Hazen region. The park index does not resolve this complete western valley corridor or its material tributary/ice links. No nearby hydronym discovered in a snippet is accepted as this feeder’s name.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeast turn and approach to the southwest lake sector
correspondence.finding: The selected turn approaches the southwest end of the Lake Hazen waterbody depicted on the park index. The actual feeder-to-lake connector and intervening major links remain unresolved in original cartography. General proximity to the lake does not establish this connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Long central and eastern lake-oriented passage
correspondence.finding: The elongated southwest-to-northeast waterbody on the original park index is labelled Lake Hazen and corresponds broadly to the long modeled lake-oriented passage. This is a lake-context observation. The index does not establish precise passage boundaries, every island/branch, the inlet transfer or a whole-route river name.

correspondence.component_scope: Southeast terminal corridor and actual selected end
correspondence.finding: The selected geometry bends southeast from the eastern lake region toward the stored sea endpoint. The park index shows only coarse water lines toward the eastern fiord system. No inspected original establishes the whole selected outlet corridor, the actual terminal branch or its hydronym at adequate ordinary component scale. The stored sea class is retained model metadata, not proof of an observed river mouth.
